words.gloss: knower of the ways of the world
endowed with self, material and constituent elements
by way of the agreeable and beneficial

hindi: लोकव्यवहार को जानने वाला व्यक्ति आत्मवान् और द्रव्य-प्रकृतियों से सम्पन्न राजा का आश्रय प्रिय और हित के द्वारा ले।
english: One who knows the ways of the world should resort to a king endowed with self-possession and the material constituent elements, by way of what is agreeable and beneficial.
notes: ātma-dravya-prakṛti-sampanna is read as 'endowed with self (self-possession) and the material constituent elements (dravya-prakṛti)', following the pairing in unit 2 (dravya-prakṛti-hīna / anātma-sampanna); other analyses are possible. loka-yātrā = the course of worldly affairs (literally 'world-journey'). dvāra = door, hence means.

hindi: अथवा जिसके विषय में वह सोचे, "जैसे मैं आश्रय चाहता हूँ, वैसे ही यह विनय चाहता है और अभिगमन के योग्य गुणों से युक्त है", उसका द्रव्य-प्रकृतियों से हीन होने पर भी आश्रय ले, किन्तु जो आत्मसम्पन्न नहीं है उसका कभी नहीं।
english: Or [the king] whom he thinks of: "Just as I desire shelter, so this one desires discipline and is endowed with approachable qualities" — even one lacking the material constituent elements he should resort to, but certainly not one who is not endowed with self-possession.
notes: ābhigāmika-guṇa = qualities of approachability (literal; ābhigāmika 'pertaining to approaching'); the sense of vinaya here (discipline/training/modesty) is not certain. The closing iti ends the quotation and is not rendered. 'The king' is supplied in brackets in English (yam is the object of manyeta). anātma-sampanna is read as na-ātma-sampanna 'not endowed with self-possession'; ana-ātma 'one without self' is possible.

words.gloss: from hatred of the treatise on policy

hindi: अनात्मवान् नीतिशास्त्र के प्रति द्वेष से अथवा निरर्थक के संयोग से महान् ऐश्वर्य को पाकर भी नहीं होता।
english: One who is not self-possessed, through hatred of the treatise on policy or through association with the worthless, even having obtained great sovereignty, does not come to be.

text_flags.why: nom. sg. of a -vat stem is -vān; the final n seems to have been lost in typing (possible)

notes: The predicate 'na bhavati' has no complement; rendered literally. Commentators/translators supply a sense such as 'does not keep/prosper in it'; not applied. anarthya = worthless (also possible: harmful, useless); the same word is rendered 'worthless' in unit 14. aiśvarya = sovereignty/lordship.

hindi: आत्मवान् के प्रति अवसर पाकर शास्त्र की शिक्षा दे।
english: With a self-possessed [king], having found an opportunity, he should give instruction in the treatise.
notes: anuyoga is literally 'questioning, pursuing, exhortation'; 'instruction' is chosen from the context (alternative: inquiry/exposition on the treatise). The same word is rendered 'inquiry' in unit 7. 'King' is supplied in brackets in English only.

hindi: क्योंकि अविसंवाद से स्थान की स्थिरता प्राप्त करता है।
english: For by consistency he obtains steadiness of position.

text_flags.why: the e-text writes dd + hi; sandhi t+h gives -d dhi, so the aspirate belongs to hi (possible; src kept)

notes: avisaṃvāda = absence of contradiction/discrepancy (consistency, trustworthiness). sthāna = position, standing (also place).

hindi: मन्त्रणा के विषयों में पूछे जाने पर वर्तमान में और भविष्य में जो धर्म और अर्थ से युक्त और समर्थ हो, उसे निपुण पुरुष की तरह, सभा से न डरने वाला होकर कहे।
english: Asked in matters of counsel, he should say, for the present and for the future, [what is] connected with dharma and wealth, [and] capable, like a skilled man, not afraid of the assembly.

text_flags.why: pṛṣṭha means 'back'; the p.p.p. of √prach 'asked' is pṛṣṭa (cf. pṛṣṭaḥ in unit 12), so ṭh is a probable typo for ṭ

notes: samartha has no stated noun; the object of kathayet is not expressed, so the Hindi and English supply a bare relative/neutral. samartha could also be 'adequate/feasible'. mati = thought, counsel; artha rendered 'wealth' as in the glossary pair dharma-artha.

words.gloss: among those allied with the powerful

hindi: अभीष्ट होने पर वह शर्त रखे, "धर्म और अर्थ की जाँच, अविशिष्ट लोगों में, बलवान् से जुड़े हुओं में दण्ड धारण, मेरे सम्पर्क में और वर्तमान में दण्ड धारण — यह तुम न करना; मेरे पक्ष, आजीविका और गुप्त बात को हानि न पहुँचाना; और संकेत से मैं तुम्हें काम, क्रोध और दण्ड देने के विषयों में रोकूँगा"।
english: Desired [by the king], he should stipulate: "You should not [do] this: the inquiry into dharma and wealth, the wielding of punishment among the undistinguished [and] among those allied with the powerful, [and] the wielding of punishment in association with me and in the present; you should not injure my side, livelihood or secret; and by a sign I would restrain you in matters of desire, anger and punishings."
notes: Obscure sentence; rendered literally, confidence low. The grouping of the accusatives (anuyogam ... daṇḍa-dhāraṇam ... daṇḍa-dhāraṇam) as the object of 'iti na kuryāḥ' is uncertain, as is the syntax of aviśiṣṭeṣu balavat-saṃyukteṣu (could be 'among equals' / 'among those allied with the strong'). dhāraṇa = holding, wielding. anuyoga: see unit 4. The first iti closes the quoted list of prohibitions, the last iti closes the whole quotation; neither is rendered. 'By the king' in īpsitaḥ is supplied in brackets.

hindi: आदेश पाकर, अनुमति पाकर निर्दिष्ट भूमि में प्रवेश करे और बगल में, न निकट न दूर, दूसरे के आसन पर बैठे।
english: Directed [and] permitted, he should enter on the ground assigned, and should sit at the side, [neither] near [nor] far, on another's seat.
notes: sannikṛṣṭa-viprakṛṣṭa literally 'near-far'; 'neither near nor far' is the natural sense but the 'neither/nor' is supplied. para-āsana is obscure: literally 'the other's seat' (the king's? an adjacent/other seat? a seat assigned by the other); alternatives not applied. Note upaviśet with accusative = 'sit on'.

hindi: विवाद करते हुए बोलना, असभ्य, अप्रत्यक्ष, अविश्वसनीय और असत्य वाक्य, जहाँ परिहास नहीं वहाँ ऊँचे स्वर में हँसी, और शब्द करते हुए वायु और थूकना — न करे।
english: He should not make contentious speaking, [or] indecent, not-evident, unbelievable and false speech, [or] loud laughter at what is no jest, [or] noisy wind and spitting.
notes: vāta-ṣṭhīvane and śabdavatī are read as neuter dual accusatives (dvandva 'wind and spittle', 'both noisy'); vāta here is the wind of the body (breaking wind) by context, kept literal. apratyakṣam = not evident/not directly perceived. anarmaṇi (a-narman 'no jest') could also be read as an adverbial 'without occasion for jest'.

words.gloss: of the arrogant and of tricksters
request for a display of the excess of jewels
twisting of one eye and the lip
the action of knitting the brows
with those who look at women
those cast out by the hated party

hindi: दूसरे के साथ एकान्त में बात करना, लोगों की चर्चा में जोड़ी बनाकर बात करना, राजा का तथा उद्धतों और धूर्तों का वेश, रत्नों की उत्कृष्टता के प्रदर्शन का अनुरोध, एक आँख और होंठ का विकार, भौंहें चढ़ाना और बोलने वाले के प्रति वाक्य को ठुकराना, बलवान् से जुड़े हुए का विरोध, स्त्रियों, स्त्रियों को देखने वालों, पड़ोसी सामन्तों के दूतों, द्वेष्य पक्ष द्वारा निकाले हुओं और याचकों से मेलजोल, एक ही प्रयोजन के लिए साथ चलना और भीड़ — इनसे बचे।
english: He should avoid: speaking privately with another; speaking in pairs in public talk; the dress of the king and of the arrogant and of tricksters; requesting a display of the excess of jewels; twisting one eye and the lip, knitting the brows, and casting aside speech at one who speaks; opposition to one allied with the powerful; association with women, with those who look at women, with envoys of neighbouring chiefs, with those cast out by the hated party, and with petitioners; going about for one purpose; and the crowd.

text_flags.why: a space stands where the compound mark '.' is expected; compare balavat.saṃyukteṣu in unit 7 (possible)

notes: Long list of things to avoid; many members are obscure, so rendered literally (low confidence): ratna-atiśaya-prakāśa-abhyarthanam (excess/surpassing quality of jewels?), eka-akṣi-oṣṭha-nirbhogam (nirbhoga = bending, twisting), vākya-avakṣepaṇa (throwing aside, disdaining speech), strī-darśin (those who look at/see women; alt. 'who see through women'), arthya (petitioners; alt. 'those with business', 'useful ones'), dveṣya-pakṣa-avakṣipta (alt. 'thrown out by the party of the hated one'), saṅghāta (crowd; alt. combination). 'balavat saṃyukta-virodham' is read as the compound balavat-saṃyukta-virodha 'opposition to one allied with the strong'; if balavat is a separate adverb the sense differs. Whether dvandva-kathanam is 'talking in pairs' or 'talking about disputes' is uncertain.

hindi: समय को न चूकते हुए राजा का प्रयोजन, अपना प्रयोजन प्रिय और हित के साथ, और दूसरे का प्रयोजन देश और काल में कहे, जो धर्म और अर्थ से युक्त हो।
english: Without missing the time, he should speak of the king's interest, of his own interest together with the agreeable and beneficial, and of another's interest, in place and time, [what is] connected with dharma and wealth.
notes: artha rendered 'interest' (matter, concern) in the first three members and 'wealth' in dharma-artha. deśa-kāle: idiom for 'in the right place and time'; rendered literally. dharma-artha-saṃhitam may agree with the objects (the interests) rather than a separate 'what is'.

hindi: पूछे जाने पर प्रिय और हितकर कहे; अहितकर प्रिय न कहे; अथवा अप्रिय हितकर कहे, सुनने वाले और सहमत के प्रति एकान्त में।
english: Asked, he should speak the agreeable and beneficial; he should not speak the unbeneficial, agreeable; or he should speak the disagreeable, beneficial, in private, [to one] who is listening [and] approving.
notes: śṛṇvataḥ anumataḥ are genitives (or ablatives) of the person addressed; 'to one' is supplied in brackets. They may also be read as a locative-absolute-like phrase 'when he is listening and has consented'.

hindi: अथवा उत्तर देने में चुप रहे और वेश्या आदि का वर्णन न करे। अप्रिय भी निपुण हो सकते हैं, जो बाहर निकाले गए हैं, उस भाव के कारण।
english: Or he should be silent in reply, and should not describe courtesans and the like. Even the disliked may be capable, because of that state, those who have been cast out.

text_flags.why: veṣya is not a regular word here; 'courtesan' is veśya/veśyā from √viś (possible)

notes: Second half is obscure: tad-bhāva 'that state' is unclear (state of being cast out?), and the relative 'ye bahiṣkṛtāḥ' has no stated correlative; rendered literally. The sentence continues in unit 14 (anarthyāś ca priyā dṛṣṭāḥ ...).

words.gloss: following the knowledge of the mind
in what is to be laughed at

hindi: और अनर्थ्य प्रिय देखे गए हैं, जो चित्त के ज्ञान का अनुसरण करने वाले हैं। हँसने योग्य बातों में हँसे और भयंकर हँसी से बचे।
english: And the worthless are seen to be dear, those who follow the knowledge of the mind. He should laugh at what is to be laughed at, and should avoid terrible laughs.
notes: anarthya rendered 'worthless' as in unit 3 (alt. 'harmful', 'useless'); unit 10 has arthya 'petitioners' (alt. 'useful'), so the pair is uncertain. citta-jñāna-anuvartin: 'conforming to (the king's) perception of the mind' is possible. Continues from unit 13.

hindi: दूसरे से आई कठोर बात का संक्रमण कराए और दूसरों के प्रति कठोर बात न कहे। अपनी भी सहन करे, पृथ्वी के समान क्षमाशील होकर।
english: He should cause the harsh [thing] to pass from another, and should not speak harshly to others. He should endure [harshness] of his own as well, forbearing, like the earth.
notes: saṅkrāmayet (transfer/cause to pass over) is obscure here: 'pass it on', 'let it pass over him' or 'turn it away' are all possible; rendered literally. pare is locative plural of para, read 'to others' (the form could be nominative plural 'the others'). ātmanaḥ is genitive 'of himself, his own'; the supplied noun is in brackets.

words.gram: m. inst. sg. pres. part. vi-√jñā

words.gloss: of those who live by the king

hindi: क्योंकि जानने वाले को सदा पहले अपनी रक्षा करनी चाहिए; राजा पर निर्भर रहने वालों की जीविका अग्नि में जैसी कही गई है।
english: For protection of oneself should always be done first by one who discerns; for the livelihood of those who live by the king is declared as if in fire.

text_flags.why: a compound member should be the stem rāja-, not rājā (possible; sandhi would give rājopajīvinām)

notes: vṛttī is vṛttiḥ before the following r- (visarga sandhi: -iḥ r- becomes -ī r-). The following word therefore begins with r, which agrees with rāja-/rājā; the e-text 'rājā-' is taken as the stem rāja-.

hindi: अग्नि एक अंश को जलाती है, अथवा चरम तक पहुँचकर शरीर को; किन्तु राजा पुत्र और स्त्री सहित मरवा दे अथवा समृद्ध करे।
english: Fire would burn one part, or the body, having gone to the extreme; but a king would have [him] killed together with son and wife, or would cause [him] to prosper.
notes: 'paraṃ gataḥ' is uncertain (gone beyond / to the extreme / far). ardhayeta from √ardh 'to prosper' (ardhayati 'makes prosper'); alt. 'make half'. The object 'him' is supplied in brackets; the verbs are optative with no object stated.
